“Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low,” but the Committee highlights weak business fixed investment and exports and inflation running below 2 percent, alongside low market-based inflation compensation. In the literature, business fixed investment is central to business cycle dynamics and often explains a large share of real GDP slowdowns (investment function influences firms; investment spending accounted for declines in real GDP), so this weakness materially tempers the otherwise positive labor-market tone. The 25 bp rate cut and operations to maintain ample reserves align with evidence that monetary policy can support real activity via lower real rates and improved financial conditions (B. Friedman; McCallum and Nelson, 1999). With inflation expectations playing a key role in price dynamics (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Svensson), below-target inflation and subdued compensation measures justify accommodation without near-term overheating risk. Net sentiment is mildly positive but clearly risk-aware due to investment and external-sector softness.
